decisions.reason: The plug-in line extends the firm's established data integration offer, has its own web page signalling visible commitment, and has several models already invested in, so management will persist.

The building digital twin service fits the announced direction of integrating geospatial IT with enterprise systems, and any slow uptake can be attributed to a market that is still emerging, which justifies continuing.

The authentication delegation service sits close to the core offer and supports the firm's integrated solutions, so the sunk development effort and low running cost favour keeping it despite only a passing mention on the website.
The open GIS framework embodies the firm's stated strategy of open, extensible components and is a multi-model line tied to its standards work, making it central and costly to abandon.

The identity and access service for GIS applications complements the framework and the firm's managed operations, so management sees it as part of the platform commitment and attributes modest visibility to the early stage.
